text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature and location of your chest pain, and tell me how long you've been experiencing the vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your inability to speak and the severe chest pain after forceful retching, I am immediately concerned for a ruptured esophagus. I will request a Chest X-ray and CT scan of the chest to look for signs of mediastinal air or fluid. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-ray shows free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation. CT Chest results are not available in the current data. Vital signs indicate a heart rate of 107 bpm and blood pressure of 90/68 mmHg. Physical exam reveals a crunching, rasping sound on auscultation and possible crepitus on palpation of the chest and neck.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of your history, the crunching heart sounds, and the confirmed mediastinal air on your X-ray strongly points to a Boerhaave syndrome, or esophageal rupture. I must act immediately to stabilize you and prepare for surgical intervention. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture).
